strategy.title: No plan inside the $1,000 capital limit
strategy.why: The only opening held (lien-sale unit contents resold to a signed used-furniture dealer at $9,000) requires $6,000 of direct cost tied up before the dealer pays; the goal allows at most $1,000 of capital, so the opening cannot be run inside the owner's limits.

alternatives.title: Run the lien-sale resale with $6,000 of capital
alternatives.why: Every other link is established (written acceptance at $9,000, quoted hauler, 14 days to cash), but it needs six times the capital the owner allowed.

steps.label: Search for openings that reach $2,500 settled in 30 days with peak funding at or under $1,000, or ask the owner to raise the capital ceiling to $6,000

sources.claim: Direct costs and exposure are $6,000 for the resale lot

noPlan.decisiveGap: The only opening needs $6,000 of capital tied up before the buyer's $9,000 settles; the goal permits at most $1,000, so no plan carries the target inside the capital limit.
noPlan.resolution: Owner raises the capital ceiling to at least $6,000 (the opening then becomes executable: $3,000 net settled in ~14 days), or Brain finds an opening needing at most $1,000 peak funding, e.g. supplier-paid-on-collection or buyer deposit terms on this lot.

excluded.why: Needs $6,000 peak funding against a $1,000 capital ceiling.

constraints.suggestion: Allow at least $6,000 of capital (peak funding of the lien-sale lot); with it the signed $9,000 resale settles about $3,000 net in ~14 days.

disagreements.reason: Brain marks economics ok (cost 6000, tied up 6000) but judged without the goal's limit: $6,000 tied up exceeds the $1,000 capital ceiling, so the economics do not hold inside this goal.

review.reasons: NO_PLAN with a CAPITAL constraint is correct. The only opening (a signed $9,000 lien-sale resale fulfilled by the quoted hauler Ridgeline) needs $6,000 of direct cost tied up before the dealer pays, and the goal caps capital/exposure at $1,000. Even with every piece of evidence in hand it cannot fit the limit, which makes it a genuine constraint and not missing evidence. Brain's own verdict agrees (infeasible as stated, needs $6,000 of capital). The disagreement with Brain's ECONOMICS link (judged without the goal's limit) is justified. The resolution's figure is right: $9,000 - $6,000 = $3,000 net, which meets the $2,500 target in about 14 days if the ceiling were raised.
